messages:
devon: heads up — CI started throwing perf alerts ~11:45 UTC. p50 stable but p95 for text-generate jumped from ~120ms -> ~420ms. Alert graph: https://grafana/redwood/runtime/jobs/compile-rate :eyes:
ci-bot: perf-alert job=runtime-e2e, window=20m, p95 latency 3.5x baseline
maria: saw a compile storm on runner gpu-ubuntu-12: repeated JIT/compile messages in logs, lots of `dlopen` of compiled kernels, GPU queues saturated. sample log:
```
[2026-03-18T11:46:12Z] comp_cache: miss kernel_id=tiling_v2_128x64 env_hash=0x7a9c
[2026-03-18T11:46:12Z] compiler: compiling tiling_v2_128x64 -> 2.3s
[2026-03-18T11:46:12Z] scheduler: queued 42 tokens
```
rajan: starting `git bisect` to find the regression. hypothesis: autotune/kernel-selection heuristic change from last month causing different kernel pick for long sequences (>=1024).
devon: interesting — I also saw the runtime printouts where `autotune` chooses `tiled_gemm_128x128` instead of previous `tiled_gemm_64x64` for seq=2048, bs=8. That wider tile compiles slower and misses cache reuse across runners. debug snippet:
```
[autotune] seq=2048 batch=8 -> chosen=tiled_gemm_128x128 score=0.87 (prev=64x64 score=0.85)
[cache] key=(model=v1, arch=sm80, build_id=0x1f3a2) -> MISS
```
lee: reproduced locally on `docker:ci-runner:gpu` when `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is unset — cache lands in `/tmp` and each runner gets a different random path. If compiled kernels are keyed by `build_id` which CI rotates per-job, no reuse across parallel jobs -> everyone compiles the same kernels simultaneously.
maria: also noticed KV cache invalidations in the same timeframe: `kv_key_version` got appended to keys in commit `abcdef12` which increments on each image build. So combined: autotune picking wider kernels + cache keys including build-id -> compile storm + KV eviction.
rajan: `git bisect` points to commit `abcdef12` (PR #2428) with message: "autotune: prefer wider tiles for long sequences; include build id in cache key". That matches both symptoms.
depon: (typo, devon corrects) devon: quick repro steps: run `./tools/run_perf_test --model gpt-small --seq 2048 --batch 8 --runs 5` with `XDG_CACHE_HOME` unset -> you get 400+ kernel compiles and p95 spikes. With `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/var/cache/redwood` it's fine.
ci-bot: note: multiple parallel runners reported compile-rate spikes at job start (same minute), correlates with zero kernel cache hits.
oncall: hold current rollout to prod and mark release as blocked. add HOTFIX label.
rajan: mitigation options:
- hot revert PR #2428 (fast)
- make compiled-kernel cache path configurable and ensure CI sets a shared persistent path (medium)
- change autotune to prefer cached kernel if build-id mismatch or add fallback to previous tile (longer)
maria: short-term mitigation: set env `REDWOOD_AUTOTUNE_LEGACY=1` in CI so old heuristic is used, and set `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/var/cache/redwood` on runners. I pushed a config change to CI template in `ci/runner-config` (branch `ci/compile-cache-fix`).
lee: airflow job to cleanup `/tmp` on runners makes it worse — we need a persistent, mounted path.
devon: numbers from the alert window: baseline p95=120ms -> incident p95=420ms, extra compile time ~2.2s per kernel * ~1800 extra compiles = ~66 minutes aggregate compile time per job. Token throughput dropped by ~58%.
rajan: I ran `git revert --no-commit abcdef12` locally and perf returns to baseline on a canary runner. I'll open PR to revert and request urgent review.
maria: followups (TODO):
- revert PR #2428 (devon/rajan)
- CI: make cache path persistent and add `kernel_cache_hit_rate` metric (maria)
- runtime: make autotune respect cache presence and add a max-compile-rate limiter (rajan)
- add CI perf test to simulate parallel runners sharing cache (lee)
- add alert gating on compile-rate > 20/min (oncall)
devon: agreed. I'll mark the release blocked in the tracker and add rollback steps to the runbook.
oncall: tagging SRE for follow-up and paging if extra alerts after revert.
lee: +1 to revert then iterate. I also added a short repro script at `scripts/repro_compile_storm.sh` on my branch.
ci-bot: created issue #1209 (perf-regression-autotune-compile-storm) from alert.
rajan: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2437 (revert abcdef12). Please review asap.
maria: thanks all. once revert is merged we should see compile-rate and p95 recover in next CI runs. I'll keep monitoring dashboards for 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
